skill.name: onboarding
skill.description: Plan post-signup onboarding improvements with activation goals, shorter setup flows, checklists, empty states, and retention measurement.
skill.summary: Audit onboarding friction and design a shorter path to meaningful product value.

content.value_statement: New users often leave before experiencing meaningful product value. This skill helps identify onboarding friction and plan measurable improvements to activation and retention.
actual_capabilities: Structure onboarding audits with findings, impact, recommendations, and priorities.
Compare five activation models and explain trial pricing tradeoffs using whole-funnel conversion.
Design shorter post-signup flows with activation goals, checklists, empty state copy, and email triggers.
Recommend cohort definitions that separate early activation events from later retention outcomes.
Suggest experiments for flow simplification, personalization, guided experiences, and stalled user recovery.
Define measurement plans covering activation rate, time to activation, step completion, and retention.
limitations: Provides recommendations rather than deploying interfaces, configuring analytics, or sending onboarding emails.
Needs product context and reliable funnel or cohort data to assess actual onboarding performance.
Does not establish causal effects from correlations or guarantee conversion and retention improvements.
Focuses on post-signup onboarding; signup optimization and detailed ongoing email sequences are separate topics.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Activation Improvements
use_cases.description: Review a trial funnel, identify setup friction, and prioritize changes that help new accounts reach meaningful value.

use_cases.title: Design a Useful First Session
use_cases.description: Create a focused first-run flow with a short checklist, helpful empty states, and optional guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan Stalled User Recovery
use_cases.description: Define inactivity criteria and coordinate email, in-app prompts, and human outreach around incomplete activation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a First-Run Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Review onboarding for [product] serving [audience]. After signup, users complete [steps]. Identify friction and recommend one clear first-session outcome.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: assess an existing onboarding flow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Checklist and Empty State
prompt_templates.prompt: Design onboarding for [product] with activation goal [goal]. Create a three-to-seven-item checklist, empty state copy, and a primary action. Make optional guidance dismissible.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: translate an activation goal into interface recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Activation Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare activation models for [product, audience, price, and setup complexity]. Assess credit-card tradeoffs using visitor-to-paid conversion and retained customer economics. Propose the shortest meaningful onboarding path.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: choose how users experience value before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Activation and Plan an Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [anonymized cohort data], evaluate [candidate activation event]. Define early and later outcome windows, eligible denominators, and uncertainty. Propose an experiment measuring retention and customer conversion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate an activation hypothesis without confusing correlation with causation.

output_examples.input: New project management users see a blank dashboard and leave before creating a project.
output: Finding: The dashboard offers no clear first action.
Impact: New users must work out how to begin before experiencing value.
Recommendation: Add a Create Project action and an optional starter template.
Measurement: Track first-project creation and later retention using separate windows and fully observed signup cohorts.

output_examples.input: Design a short onboarding flow for a design collaboration tool.
output: Proposed activation goal: Share a design and receive the first teammate comment.
Checklist: Upload a design, invite one teammate, and request feedback.
Empty state copy: Upload a design to start collecting feedback.
Recovery trigger: Offer help when a design is uploaded but no teammate is invited within 24 hours.
Measurement: Compare time to first feedback and later retention before adopting this activation definition.

best_practices: Share the product audience, current onboarding steps, and anonymized funnel data before requesting recommendations.
Define a meaningful activation hypothesis and measure it before a separate retention outcome window.
Test prioritized changes with complete cohort follow-up and customer conversion or retention outcomes.
anti_patterns: Treating checklist completion or signup volume as proof of lasting product value.
Forcing long tours or nonessential setup before users can complete one useful action.
Applying benchmark claims or correlation thresholds as universal guarantees without product-specific validation.

faq.question: What part of the customer journey does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers post-signup onboarding, first-session value, activation, and stalled user recovery. Signup form optimization is a separate topic.

faq.question: Does it implement onboarding changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It produces audits, flow recommendations, copy, experiment ideas, and measurement plans. Implementation requires your product team or separate tools.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the product audience, value proposition, onboarding steps, suspected activation event, and available funnel or cohort data. Use anonymized data.

faq.question: Can it help choose between freemium and a trial?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares freemium, free trials, paid trials, money-back guarantees, and consultation models against market needs and customer economics.

faq.question: Can it prove that an activation event causes retention?
faq.answer: No. It treats correlations as hypotheses and recommends separate measurement windows, mature cohorts, and experiments to evaluate causal effects.

faq.question: Does it require an analytics account or API key?
faq.answer: The skill declares no analytics account or API key requirement. It can use supplied context and optionally read a local product marketing document.
